categories.name: Geopolitical & conflict

sources.title: Haaretz: Iran says Hormuz will stay closed until US meets demands
PBS: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz over US blockade

categories.summary: Overnight searches found no new confirmed attacks. Iran still says Hormuz stays closed until the US lifts its blockade, and only a couple of ships a day are getting through. Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no new warning signs; a Russian drone briefly closed Moldova's airspace, which does not affect us.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal. Forecast markets on a Russian nuclear test rose slightly to about 4%, still low.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure

sources.title: TechCrunch: US government warns of ongoing cyber threat to freezers
Yahoo/WSJ: Iran expands cyberattacks with greater real-world impact

categories.summary: Hackers suspected of working for Iran have hit small US water stations, systems on two tankers headed for Texas, and freezers in Europe and at US military bases. US cyber agencies warned of the freezer campaign on 5 November, but no government has officially blamed Iran yet. A criminal gang also breached Optimizely, which runs parts of many big brand websites. Separately, the US flight halt, Microsoft and Chase outages were faults, not hacks. Nothing has been reported in Australia, and our banks, phones and grid are normal.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological

sources.title: WHO: Ebola (Bundibugyo) - DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

categories.summary: WHO reports Ebola continuing in parts of Africa, MERS in Qatar and Saudi Arabia, and a pneumonia of unknown cause in Russia; none is spreading toward Australia. Adelaide emergency departments are not unusually busy.

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: Fire danger is Moderate in the Hills today and tomorrow with no fire bans or CFS warnings. Grass fires near Truro and elsewhere had no warnings. Friday looks windier (gusts near 53 km/h). A magnitude 6.6 quake in the Banda Sea (north of Darwin) caused no tsunami.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply
categories.summary: Hormuz still carries only about 2 ships a day (100+ before the war). Brent oil is about US$93, and in Aussie dollars it is up about 3% on a week ago. The Philippines has declared an energy emergency; Australia's supply is tight but there are no shortages in SA.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: The VIX fear gauge rose about 13% to near 26, jumpy but not alarming. The Australian dollar slipped to about 67.4 US cents, which makes fuel dearer. Gold and oil edged up.

headline: Iran is still keeping Hormuz shut over the US blockade, which keeps fuel dear, but nothing new happened overnight that needs action.
summary: No new attacks in the Gulf overnight; the Hormuz standoff that keeps fuel prices high is unchanged. Hackers suspected of working for Iran are hitting water, shipping and cold-storage systems in the US and Europe, and US agencies have warned about it; nothing has been reported in Australia. The big US outages this week were faults, not hacks. Locally it is calm: Moderate fire danger in the Hills, no fire bans, and the grid and phones are normal.
